newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Fighting erupts in southern Philippines, 17 killed.
newsitem.headline: Fighting erupts in southern Philippines, 17 killed.

text.p: At least 17 people have died in fresh fighting between government troops and the Moslem fundamentalist Abu Sayyaf group on a southern Philippine island, an Army spokesman said on Saturday.

Army Captain Salih Indanan told reporters that about 12 Abu Sayyaf and five army rangers were killed during a fierce gunbattle on Friday in Lantawan town on Basilan island, 900 km (600 miles) south of Manila.
Four other soldiers were still missing.
The military had been following up a tip that more than 40 armed members of the extremist group had landed in Basilan earlier in the week.
"We expect the offensive operation against these terrorists will continue (now that) our troops have positively pinpointed their lairs," Indanan said.

Members of Abu Sayyaf are held responsible for a series of terrorist attacks and kidnappings in southern Mindanao island. They are not included in the peace process being conducted by the government with the mainstream Moslem rebels.
Last Thursday, the government declared a four-day unilateral ceasefire with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front to allow for a resumption of peace talks.
